extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of moral/social essays and character sketches (early-18th-century literary audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and evaluative points for composing moralizing essays and character portraits: how to teach by example, portray virtues/characters, and use stylistic devices in narrative and epic works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach by exemplar (stories over rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Man improves more by reading the Story of a Person eminent for Prudence and Virtue, than by the finest Rules and Precepts of Morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer presenting concrete stories of exemplary persons rather than abstract maxims; narrative exemplars make a stronger impression and better instruct readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach by negative example (calamities of the weak)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Representation of those Calamities and Misfortunes which a weak Man suffers from wrong Measures, and ill-concerted Schemes of Life, is apt to make a deeper Impression upon our Minds, than the wisest Maxims and Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use depictions of error and misfortune to illustrate consequences and instruct readers; showing failures can be more persuasive than stating precepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present material and let readers draw conclusions (avoid authorial moralizing)
rubrics_metrics.description: I lay before my Reader the following Letter, and leave it with him to make his own use of it, without adding any Reflections of my own upon the Subject Matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow the narrative or example to speak for itself; resist heavy-handed postscript moralizing—trust readers to infer lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveal character through domestic/habitual detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Character is shown by changes in household, manners, dress and daily conduct (e.g., turning off long-serving servants, introducing foreign attendants, glazing chimneypieces with looking-glass, weekly illuminations, footmen's affectations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, domestic particulars and recurring habits to expose social pretensions and a character's true priorities—show not tell via behaviors and household changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine external beauty with internal virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: As Virtue makes a beautiful Woman appear more beautiful, so Beauty makes a virtuous Woman really more virtuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray beauty and wisdom together: external attractiveness should be balanced and enhanced by inner moral qualities rather than presented as the sole value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray virtue as decency and unstudied grace rather than severity
rubrics_metrics.description: The unstudied Graces of her Behaviour... Thus, tho the Attractives of her Beauty play almost irresistibly upon you and create Desire, you immediately stand corrected not by the Severity but the Decency of her Virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict moral excellence through natural, modest behavior and tone rather than through austere or preachy displays—decency and restrained charm are persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray religion as reasoned, consistent, compassionate
rubrics_metrics.description: Religion in Emilia is a Principle founded in Reason and enlivened with Hope; it does not break forth into irregular Fits and Sallies of Devotion... It is strict without Severity, compassionate without Weakness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting piety, emphasize a stable, rational, humane practice of religion rather than ostentation, fear, melancholy, or mere ritual formality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuade by example, not lectures
rubrics_metrics.description: A silent Example and an easie unrepining Behaviour, will always be more perswasive than the Severity of Lectures and Admonitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In character development and moral instruction, use the character's actions and demeanor to influence others rather than direct didactic speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor, realistic details matter (dress and neatness affect relationships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrapping Gowns and dirty Linnen... I have often thought wrapping Gowns and dirty Linnen ... the Bane of conjugal Love, and one of the readiest Means imaginable to alienate the Affection of an Husband.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not dismiss small, everyday particulars as mere trifles; such details shape intimacy, social perception, and character dynamics and should be used purposefully in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match exposition style to subject (plain/simple exordium for epic)
rubrics_metrics.description: These Lines are perhaps as plain, simple and unadorned as any of the whole Poem, in which Particular the Author has conformed himself to the Example of Homer and the Precept of Horace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a style of opening appropriate to the work's scale and tradition—classical plainness suits grand epic exordia; conformity to exemplary models can be a virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose an invocation appropriate to the poem's source and subject
rubrics_metrics.description: His Invocation to a Work which turns in a great measure upon the Creation of the World, is very properly made to the Muse who inspired Moses... and to the Holy Spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select invocations or framing devices that align logically and thematically with the poem's sources and subject matter to strengthen coherence and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use noble language and provide natural transition to the fable
rubrics_metrics.description: This whole Exordium rises very happily into noble Language and Sentiment, as I think the Transition to the Fable is exquisitely beautiful and natural.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft an exordium that elevates tone and creates a smooth, organic move into the narrative or fable; diction and sentiment should suit the grandeur of the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ striking imaginative devices to heighten wonder (e.g., 'Nine Days Astonishment')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nine Days Astonishment, in which the Angels lay entranced after their dreadful Overthrow and Fall from Heaven, before they could recover either the use of Thought or Speech, is a noble Circumstance, and very finely imagined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prolonged, imaginative conceits or grand set-pieces to amplify emotional impact and wonder; such devices can be memorable and effective when well-conceived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive world-building and moral topology enhance epic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Hell into Seas of Fire, and into firm Ground impregnated with the same furious Element, with that particular Circumstance of the Exclusion of Hope from those Infernal Regions, are Instances of the same great and fruitful Invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create distinctive, morally meaningful settings and structural conceits in imaginative works; inventive topographies and moral rules (e.g., absence of hope) deepen thematic resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce major characters by speeches that interweave passions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Thoughts in the first Speech and Description of Satan... His Pride, Envy and Revenge, Obstinacy, Despair and Impenitence, are all of them very artfully interwoven. In short, his first Speech is a Complication of all those Passions...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce key characters through speeches or actions that simultaneously display multiple, interrelated motives and traits to present psychological complexity and make them compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict age-appropriate behavior (avoid affectation beyond one's station)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are eternally pursuing the same Methods which first procured us the Applauses of Mankind... It is this, in a Word, which fills the Town with elderly Fops, and superannuated Coquets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation should respect the natural consequences of age and station: authors should avoid portraying characters who persist in incongruous affectations that render them ridiculous rather than admirable.
